:::{#cor-linearity-affine}
#### Expectation of a linear function of one random variable

For a random variable $X$ with a defined expectation,
and constants $a$ and $c$:

$$\E{aX + c} = a\E{X} + c$$

:::

::: proof

For discrete $X$, this identity is @thm-linearity-expectation with $b = 0$.
For continuous $X$ with density $\p(X=x)$,
apply @thm-lotus with $g(x) = ax + c$:

$$
\ba
\E{aX + c}
&= \int_{x \in \rangef{X}} (ax + c) \cd \p(X=x)\,dx
&& \text{(LOTUS, continuous case)} \\
&= a\int_{x \in \rangef{X}} x \cd \p(X=x)\,dx
 + c\int_{x \in \rangef{X}} \p(X=x)\,dx
&& \text{(linearity of the integral)} \\
&= a\E{X} + c\int_{x \in \rangef{X}} \p(X=x)\,dx
&& \text{(definition of expectation)} \\
&= a\E{X} + c \cd 1
&& \text{(a density integrates to 1)} \\
&= a\E{X} + c
&& \text{(simplify)}
\ea
$$

Splitting the integral is valid because both pieces converge absolutely:
the first because $\E{X}$ is defined,
and the second because its integrand is a non-negative density.

:::
